doc.title: Ira Gitler interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Joe Williams on an old Savoy LP and Every Day
summary: Gitler recalls Williams's pre-Basie Savoy recording and the Basie version of Every Day with Frank Foster obbligati.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: That’s where I was going, that’s where I was going next. Talk to us about Joe as a singer, as a cultural icon as well.

Well it’s interesting, but I was shuffling through some LPs the other night because my wife had to clean out a certain section, you know, “We’ve got to clean out, there’s too much dust over there, get these LPs out” and it happened to be the end of V through Z. And so I was looking through them naturally after we got them out. And here was Joe Williams, it’s a Savoy LP, I don’t know if it’s been re-issued on CD, and it had some of his early work, pre-Basie. And there’s a version of “Every Day” on there and it points out that he did this and the thing did nothing. So you know everything has its time and its presentation and everything came together when he made that recording with Basie. Of course I think it was Ernie Wilkin’s arrangement if I’m not mistaken, Frank Foster plays behind him, like beautiful obbligati, and the band is kicking and the thing took off. And
